Name: Torey Stevens
Badge: Reading to Write: They Say / I Say
Which version of the They Say / I Say routine (with visual texts or with annotation) feels like the best fit for your students right now? Why?:

I believe starting with the visual texts will be the best fit for my students. I believe that they will be able to develop the routine with visuals interpretation of information/arguments that then can be translated a little more easily into written texts. My goal would be to use the visuals to establish a routine first.

Describe one way you might adapt the They Say / I Say framework to align with the types of texts your students read most often (e.g., articles, visuals, multimodal texts).:

I might develop specific questions for the texts that I chose that help focus on certain standards that I am focusing on for a particular lesson. For example, I might try to adapt this for literary texts for the beginning of the school year before I get into informational/argumentative writing.

What, if anything, do you need help thinking through as you plan for using They Say / I Say in your classroom?:

I do not believe I need help with thinking through anything to use this in my class. However, I would take any helpful advice anyone has to offer.
